text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Asian countries were advised to reduce their dependence on foreign capital to finance their investment activities by raising domestic savings.
- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the 800,000 civil servants would receive their one-month bonus or a minimum of 700 ringgit each by the end of this month.
- Malaysia has proposed that regulatory authorities in the region consider making it more flexible for Asian countries to raise funds from the capital markets of other Asian countries.
- Maybank, Malaysia's largest commercial bank, has been tipped as a strong contender for a stake in the Philippine National Bank's wholly-owned commercial banking subsidiary, PNB-Republic Bank.
- Taiwan Vice Economic Minister Sheu Ke-sheng denied a report that Taiwan has suspended a three-year programme promoting investment in Southeast Asian nations.
- Three brothers died when a minor fire engulfed an illegally built attic of an extensively renovated house in Petaling Jaya on Monday.
